sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空中度过的七十年。

sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外是什么。

sentences.zh: 今天我要测试七个床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60个超级圣代。

sentences.en: I'm Lulu Garcia Navarro, and this is The Interview.
sentences.zh: 我是露露·加西亚-纳瓦罗，这里是《访谈》。

sentences.en: It's hard to overstate the impact of 60 Minutes on journalism.
sentences.zh: 《60分钟》对新闻界的影响怎么强调都不为过。

sentences.en: Since its debut on CBS in 1968, it's been the home of some of the most famous and lauded journalists,
sentences.zh: 自1968年在哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）开播以来，这里一直是许多最著名、最受赞誉的新闻工作者的家园，

sentences.en: from Mike Wallace and Ed Bradley to Leslie Stahl, Anderson Cooper, and until this past week, Scott Pelley.
sentences.zh: 从迈克·华莱士、埃德·布拉德利到莱斯利·斯塔尔、安德森·库珀，以及直到上周的斯科特·佩利。

sentences.en: Pelley was fired after an explosive series of events and much turmoil at CBS, including a controversial financial settlement with President Trump,
sentences.zh: 佩利在CBS经历了一系列爆炸性事件和巨大的动荡后被解雇，其中包括与特朗普总统达成颇具争议的财务和解、

sentences.en: the sale of the network to David Ellison, and the appointment of Barry Weiss to lead CBS News.
sentences.zh: 将电视网出售给大卫·埃里森，以及任命巴里·韦斯领导CBS新闻。

sentences.en: Pelley, along with a number of other 60 Minutes correspondents who were fired, have now accused Weiss of editorial interference and bias, charges that CBS and Weiss deny.
sentences.zh: 佩利以及其他几位被解雇的《60分钟》记者现在指控韦斯进行编辑干预和带有偏见，CBS和韦斯对此予以否认。

sentences.en: We've included a fuller statement from CBS News at the end of the episode.
sentences.zh: 我们在本集末尾附上了CBS新闻更完整的声明。

sentences.en: This is Scott Pelley's first sit-down interview since he was fired.
sentences.zh: 这是斯科特·佩利被解雇以来的首次坐下访谈。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for coming in.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您能来。

sentences.en: I know that this is a very difficult moment.
sentences.zh: 我知道这是一个非常艰难的时刻。

sentences.en: You were just fired from the news organization, which you were at the heart of for 37 years.
sentences.zh: 你刚刚被你作为核心融入了37年的新闻机构解雇。

sentences.en: I can't believe I'm hearing those words.
sentences.zh: 我简直不敢相信自己听到了这些话。

sentences.en: CBS News.
sentences.zh: CBS新闻。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I want to actually start by just asking you how you're feeling in this moment before we start how you got here.
sentences.zh: 在探讨你是如何走到这一步之前，我想先问问你此刻的感受。

sentences.en: Well, if we want to talk about it at an emotional level, the best thing that I can imagine in terms of describing it is that it's like your spouse was murdered.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果我们从情感层面来谈，我能想到的最好的描述就是，这就像你的配偶被谋杀了一样。

sentences.en: There's some moments of the day I feel fine.
sentences.zh: 一天中的某些时刻我感觉很好。

sentences.en: There are some moments of the day that I just frankly fall apart when I least expect it.
sentences.zh: 但一天中也有某些时刻，坦白说，我在最意想不到的时候彻底崩溃了。

sentences.en: Not that there's any particular trigger.
sentences.zh: 倒也不是有什么特定的导火索。

sentences.en: But I do want to be clear that I do not feel sorry for me.
sentences.zh: 但我必须澄清，我并不是在为自己感到难过。

sentences.en: I don't care about me.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎我自己。

sentences.en: I'm fine.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: I care about these people that I left behind.
sentences.zh: 我在乎的是那些被我留下的人，

sentences.en: the people who are still trapped there, and this institution that I love so much.
sentences.zh: 那些仍然被困在那里的人，以及这个我深爱至深的机构。

sentences.en: You said that I've been there 37 years.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说我在那里待了37年。

sentences.en: I've been married 42 years.
sentences.zh: 我已经结婚42年了。

sentences.en: So that's the depth of my devotion.
sentences.zh: 这就是我投入的深情。

sentences.en: Let's talk about how we got to this moment.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈是如何走到这一步的吧。

sentences.en: A few days before your firing, several high-profile 60 Minutes correspondents and leaders were fired.
sentences.zh: 在你被解雇前几天，几位备受瞩目的《60分钟》记者和领导被解雇了。

sentences.en: Leading up to that, there'd been a lot of reporting about changes that were coming to 60 Minutes.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，有很多关于《60分钟》即将迎来变革的报道。

sentences.en: Was that the sort of change you were expecting?
sentences.zh: 这正是你所期待的那种变革吗？

sentences.en: No one saw the Black Thursday massacre coming.
sentences.zh: 没有人预料到“黑色星期四”大屠杀的到来。

sentences.en: This is our entire senior staff.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的整个高层团队。

sentences.en: people beloved.
sentences.zh: 都是备受喜爱的人。

sentences.en: Tanya Simon, our executive producer, she's the boss.
sentences.zh: 我们的执行制片人坦娅·西蒙，她是老板。

sentences.en: And this was her triumph.
sentences.zh: 而这是她的辉煌成就。

sentences.en: She's the first woman ever to be executive producer of 60 Minutes.
sentences.zh: 她是《60分钟》历史上第一位女性执行制片人。

sentences.en: And she concluded this season with a growth in our audience of 9%, which is unheard of in broadcast television, and a growth in our online presence of 190%.
sentences.zh: 她带领本季节目实现了9%的观众增长，这在电视广播界是闻所未闻的，我们的在线受众更是增长了190%。

sentences.en: Last season, we had 2.5 billion views.
sentences.zh: 上一季，我们获得了25亿次的观看量。

sentences.en: That's a third of humanity.
sentences.zh: 那是全人类的三分之一。

sentences.en: So we're riding high.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正处于春风得意之时。

sentences.en: This management team has been brilliant.
sentences.zh: 这个管理团队一直非常出色。

sentences.en: Tanya has the best first year of any executive producer, and I've worked for all of them.
sentences.zh: 坦娅拥有所有执行制片人中最棒的第一年，而他们我都共事过。

sentences.en: And then the night before,
sentences.zh: 然后就在前一天晚上，

sentences.en: Tanya and I and Dragan Mihaljevic, her deputy, et cetera, were all at the Emmy Awards and we win two Emmy Awards.
sentences.zh: 坦娅和我、她的副手德拉甘·米哈莱维奇等人都在艾美奖颁奖典礼上，我们赢得了两个艾美奖。
zh_words: 副手德拉甘·米哈莱维奇

sentences.en: Within hours, all of those people have been wiped out
sentences.zh: 而在几小时内，所有人全都被清洗掉了，

sentences.en: and one third of our correspondents have been fired.
sentences.zh: 三分之一的记者被解雇了。

sentences.en: And at the same moment that that happens,
sentences.zh: 就在发生这一切的同一时刻，

sentences.en: We are informed of our new executive producer.
sentences.zh: 我们被告知了我们的新执行制片人。

sentences.en: His name is Nick Bilton.
sentences.zh: 他叫尼克·比尔顿。

sentences.en: I'm sure he must be a wonderful man, but no one had ever heard of him.
sentences.zh: 我确信他一定是个很好的人，但从来没有人听说过他。

sentences.en: He has zero experience in television news and no experience in management.
sentences.zh: 他在电视新闻方面零经验，在管理上也毫无经验。

sentences.en: So imagine how we feel when someone like that comes into a shop like 60 Minutes.
sentences.zh: 所以试想一下，当这样一个人空降到《60分钟》这样的地方时，我们的感受如何。

sentences.en: Explain to me exactly how you felt.
sentences.zh: 请向我详细解释一下你的感受。

sentences.en: Shock, dismay, impossible to believe, searching desperately for an explanation, knowing that an explanation would be forthcoming and then not seeing that.
sentences.zh: 震惊、沮丧、简直难以置信，拼命想要寻找一个解释，明知会有解释却又迟迟不见。

sentences.en: No executive at CBS News, our editor-in-chief, Barry Weiss, coming over to 60 Minutes to explain, to talk with us, to sit with us.
sentences.zh: CBS新闻没有高管，我们的总编辑巴里·韦斯，没有一个人来到《60分钟》跟我们解释，跟我们对话，坐下来谈谈。

sentences.en: That's a family at 60 Minutes.
sentences.zh: 《60分钟》是一个大家庭。

sentences.en: My colleagues and I have worked together 10, 20, 30 years.
sentences.zh: 我的同事和我一起工作了10年、20年、30年。

sentences.en: We travel together.
sentences.zh: 我们一起旅行。

sentences.en: We dine together.
sentences.zh: 我们一起用餐。

sentences.en: We go into literal combat together.
sentences.zh: 我们曾一起经历真正的战斗。

sentences.en: My former boss and former producer, Bill Owens, saved my life in a firefight in Iraq.
sentences.zh: 我的前老板兼前制作人比尔·欧文斯在伊拉克的一场交火中救了我的命。

sentences.en: So, Lulu, these bonds are pretty tight.
sentences.zh: 所以，露露，这些纽带非常深厚。

sentences.en: And when somebody wipes out, murders a large number of your family members, people are hurt and shocked in disbelief and just desperate for some explanation.
sentences.zh: 当有人消灭、谋杀了你的大量家庭成员时，人们会感到痛苦、震惊、难以置信，并且极度渴望得到某种解释。

sentences.en: And as you and I sit here today, there still has been none.
sentences.zh: 但正如你我今天坐在这里一样，依然没有任何解释。

sentences.en: CBS leadership says that they tried to get in touch with you to talk about all of those changes before Bilton's first day.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚广播公司领导层表示，在比尔顿上任的第一天之前，他们曾试图联系你，和你谈谈所有这些变动。

sentences.en: And you didn't speak to them.
sentences.zh: 而你没有和他们说话。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: I'm almost 69 years old.
sentences.zh: 我都快69岁了。

sentences.en: And if I've learned one thing in life, it is not to reflexively react when you feel that way.
sentences.zh: 如果我在生活中学到了一件事，那就是当你产生这种感觉时，不要本能地做出反应。

sentences.en: And I thought, you know, I'm going to give it a day or something.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道的，我要等上一天左右。

sentences.en: I'm too emotionally wrought up.
sentences.zh: 我的情绪太激动了。

sentences.en: I'm going to say the wrong thing.
sentences.zh: 我会说错话的。

sentences.en: I'm not going to hear what they have to say.
sentences.zh: 我也听不进他们要说的话。

sentences.en: This isn't the moment.
sentences.zh: 现在不是时候。

sentences.en: It was incredible to me that they did reach out to talk to me after wiping all these people out.
sentences.zh: 令我难以置信的是，在把这些人全都赶走之后，他们居然还联系我想谈谈。

sentences.en: I mean, within hours.
sentences.zh: 我是说，就在几个小时内。

sentences.en: so um we had a baby shower at the house and we got through the weekend and i learned that nick bilton was going to speak to the 60 minute staff on that next monday morning
sentences.zh: 所以嗯，我们在家里举办了一个迎婴派对，我们度过了那个周末，然后我得知尼克·比尔顿将在接下来的周一早上向《60分钟》的员工发表讲话

sentences.en: my wife and i uh had a long planned hiking trip in the canadian rockies planned and i wasn't going
sentences.zh: 我和我妻子呃原计划在加拿大落基山脉进行一次筹划已久的徒步旅行，而我将无法

sentences.en: to be able to be at the meeting and uh she and i talked about it realized that this was an existential moment for 60 minutes.
sentences.zh: 参加那场会议，呃她和我谈过这件事，意识到这对《60分钟》来说是一个生死存亡的时刻。

sentences.en: So we canceled the vacation so I could be there.
sentences.zh: 所以我们取消了假期，这样我才能出席。

sentences.en: And that was the first time that I had an opportunity to meet Nick Bilton.
sentences.zh: 那是我第一次有机会见到尼克·比尔顿。

sentences.en: At that meeting, you spoke up very forcefully.
sentences.zh: 在那个会议上，你发言非常有力。

sentences.en: You asked him why he'd taken the job knowing, and this is a quote, that you will never be welcome here.
sentences.zh: 你问他，既然明知——这里引用你的原话——“你永远不会在这里受欢迎”，为什么还要接下这份工作？

sentences.en: Why did you decide to have that first interaction with your new boss in public and not behind closed doors?
sentences.zh: 你为什么决定在公开场合而不是在闭门会议中与你的新老板进行第一次互动？

sentences.en: It wasn't in public.
sentences.zh: 那不是在公开场合。

sentences.en: It was behind closed doors.
sentences.zh: 那是在闭门进行。

sentences.en: I was with my family in a closed room.
sentences.zh: 我和家人在一个封闭的房间里。

sentences.en: None of this was meant to be public.
sentences.zh: 这些本都不是为了公开的。

sentences.en: But Lulu, imagine I'm walking into this room with these people who have devoted their lives to 60 Minutes.
sentences.zh: 但露露，想象一下，我走进这个房间，面对的这些人把他们的一生都奉献给了《60分钟》。

sentences.en: They have not received any kind of explanation.
sentences.zh: 他们没有收到任何形式的解释。

sentences.en: They are waiting for Barry Weiss to walk in the room in the hope that she's going to explain why this tragedy has occurred and why it was so necessary.
sentences.zh: 他们在等待巴里·韦斯走进房间，希望她能解释这场悲剧为什么会发生，以及为什么它是如此必要。

sentences.en: And I'm waiting to see who comes in, and it's Nick Bilton and one of Barry's deputies.
sentences.zh: 我正等着看谁进来，结果是尼克·比尔顿和巴里的一个副手。

sentences.en: No, Barry.
sentences.zh: 没有巴里。

sentences.en: people are a little shocked by this as we're standing in there nick makes his way to the front of the room and does something absolutely jaw-dropping to me he pulls out his phone
sentences.zh: 人们对此感到有点震惊，当我们站在那里时，尼克走到房间前面，对我做了一件绝对让人惊掉下巴的事，他掏出手机

sentences.en: and begins reading a statement off his phone in a room full of 50 heartbroken people the callousness
sentences.zh: 开始照着手机读一份声明，在一个坐满50个心碎之人的房间里，这种冷酷

sentences.en: the tone deafness of that you could hear the groan in the room when that happened
sentences.zh: 这种麻木不仁，事情发生时你能听到房间里传出一阵叹息声

sentences.en: they'd put out a big spread of bagels like we were all going to feel better and also if i can give you a little bit of context please what had happened a couple of days before
sentences.zh: 他们摆出了一大盘百吉饼，好像我们所有人都会因此感觉好一点一样，还有，如果我可以给你提供一点背景的话，请听我说，在会议召开前几天发生的事情

sentences.en: the meeting was so critical.
sentences.zh: 是至关重要的。

sentences.en: Nick Bilton wrote an email to the staff, sort of introducing himself.
sentences.zh: 尼克·比尔顿给员工写了一封邮件，算是自我介绍。

sentences.en: And it was so insulting to the staff and so insulting to the history of 60 Minutes.
sentences.zh: 那封邮件对员工是如此侮辱，对《60分钟》的历史是如此侮辱。

sentences.en: He told us in that email that it wasn't 1968 anymore.
sentences.zh: 他在邮件中告诉我们，现在已经不是1968年了。

sentences.en: And he helpfully noted that gasoline doesn't cost 32 cents anymore.
sentences.zh: 他还煞费苦心地指出，汽油已经不再是32美分了。

sentences.en: And suggested that we had all been frozen in amber in 1968 when the program first went on the air and that nothing had improved.
sentences.zh: 并暗示我们所有人在1968年这个节目首次开播时就已经被封存在琥珀里了，而且没有什么地方有所改进。

sentences.en: And he said in his email that it was, quote, strange, end quote, that 60 minutes is only on the air at seven o'clock Eastern time on Sunday once a week.
sentences.zh: 他在邮件里说，《60分钟》每周日东部时间晚上七点只播出一一次，用他的话说，是“奇怪的”。

sentences.en: When we've been on the air 24-7 globally online for well over a decade, it betrayed the fact that Nick Bilton didn't know anything about us, didn't know anything
sentences.zh: 而我们十多年来一直在全天候24小时全球在线播出，这暴露出尼克·比尔顿对我们一无所知，对我们的文化

sentences.en: about our culture, and yet was being imposed on us as our new executive producer, our new leader.
sentences.zh: 一无所知，然而却被强加给我们，作为我们的新执行制片人、我们的新领导。

sentences.en: So people read that memo.
sentences.zh: 所以人们读了那份备忘录。

sentences.en: It's very concerning.
sentences.zh: 这非常令人担忧。

sentences.en: It's heartbreaking.
sentences.zh: 这太令人心碎了。

sentences.en: It's hard to compare this to anything other than something that actually could happen to your family.
sentences.zh: 这很难与任何其他事情相比，除了那些真正会降临到你家人身上的事情。

sentences.en: It's a very loving and empathetic organization.
sentences.zh: 这是一个充满爱心和同理心的组织。

sentences.en: And we were met with cold, callous indifference to what anyone thought.
sentences.zh: 而我们得到的却是对任何人的想法的冰冷、残酷和冷漠。

sentences.en: Why did you feel that you were the person that needed to get the answers to the questions that you had and everyone had at that meeting?
sentences.zh: 为什么你觉得你就是那个必须在那个会议上找出你和所有人都想知道的答案的人？

sentences.en: Why did you feel compelled to speak up?
sentences.zh: 为什么你觉得自己责无旁贷必须站出来说话？

sentences.en: It was fate.
sentences.zh: 这是命中注定。

sentences.en: First of all, our entire senior staff had been wiped out.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们的整个高级管理层都被清除了。

sentences.en: They're not there.
sentences.zh: 他们不在那里。

sentences.en: I looked around the room.
sentences.zh: 我环顾四周。

sentences.en: I'm the only correspondent there, which surprised me very much.
sentences.zh: 我是那里唯一的记者，这让我感到非常惊讶。

sentences.en: I learned that my colleagues were out shooting stories, as they should be in the month of June.
sentences.zh: 我得知我的同事们都在外拍摄报道，就像他们在六月份应该做的那样。

sentences.en: But I'm the only correspondent there, which surprised me.
sentences.zh: 但我是那里唯一的记者，这让我很惊讶。

sentences.en: And I looked around at my friends and colleagues in the room and realized I was the senior person.
sentences.zh: 我环顾房间里的朋友和同事，意识到我是资历最高的人。

sentences.en: Only I could do it.
sentences.zh: 只有我能做到。

sentences.en: None of them could be asked to take that risk.
sentences.zh: 不能要求他们中的任何一个人去冒那个险。

sentences.en: So when I saw Nick Bilton's email and then saw him reading to my brokenhearted people off his phone,
sentences.zh: 所以当我看到尼克·比尔顿的邮件，然后又看到他对着手机向我那些心碎的人们宣读时，

sentences.en: I felt that somebody had to stand up for the broadcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我觉得必须有人站出来捍卫这个节目。

sentences.en: not just the broadcast, but the people.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是节目，还有那些人。

sentences.en: There are people in that room who go to war zones when they are pregnant.
sentences.zh: 那个房间里有些人怀孕时还会去战区。

sentences.en: Newsrooms are sort of like the military or the police or the beautiful people at the FDNY down the street.
sentences.zh: 新闻编辑室有点像军队、警察，或者街头那些消防局的英雄们。

sentences.en: It is a life-threatening job in many instances.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，这是一份危及生命的工作。

sentences.en: and very strong bonds, very emotional bonds are found or are developed in that kind of setting.
sentences.zh: 在那种环境下，人们会建立起非常深厚的纽带、非常的情感纽带。

sentences.en: And to have people running CBS News who don't know that, have never felt that and don't understand it is a tragedy I never expected to see.
sentences.zh: 让那些不了解这一点、从未感受过这一点、也不理解这一切的人来运营哥伦比亚广播公司新闻部，是我做梦也没想到会看到的悲剧。

sentences.en: You know, Barry Weiss came into the job with a mandate to evolve and modernize CBS News to reinvent legacy media.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，巴里·韦斯上任时肩负着推动和实现哥伦比亚广播公司新闻部现代化、重塑传统媒体的使命。

sentences.en: In that meeting, you said Weiss was, and I'm quoting here, murdering 60 Minutes, language that you've used here.
sentences.zh: 在那个会议上，你说韦斯，我在这里引用原话，正在“谋杀《60分钟》”，这也是你在这里使用过的语言。

sentences.en: Can you explain to me what you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你能向我解释一下你这话是什么意思吗？

sentences.en: You're using words like massacre, murder.
sentences.zh: 你用了“大屠杀”、“谋杀”这样的词。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: It was the wholesale nature of it.
sentences.zh: 主要是因为这件事的规模太庞大了。

sentences.en: Our senior staff wiped out after a triumphal year.
sentences.zh: 在我们经历了辉煌的一年之后，我们的高层管理人员却被一网打尽。

sentences.en: Let's remember that.
sentences.zh: 让我们记住这一点。

sentences.en: If the ratings had collapsed or there was some journalistic scandal about a story, then okay, we deserve it.
sentences.zh: 如果收视率崩溃了，或者关于某篇报道出现了什么新闻丑闻，那好吧，这是我们咎由自取。

sentences.en: But we had a triumphal year, so this is incredibly difficult to understand.
sentences.zh: 但我们度过了辉煌的一年，所以这实在让人难以理解。

sentences.en: Cecilia Vega, Sharon Alfonsi, our very best correspondents, just summarily fired for no stated reason and without explanation.
sentences.zh: 西莉亚·维加（Cecilia Vega）、莎朗·阿尔方西（Sharon Alfonsi），我们最优秀的记者，就这么毫无理由、不加解释地被直接解雇了。

sentences.en: This is one-third of our correspondent core.
sentences.zh: 这占了我们核心记者团队的三分之一。

sentences.en: So this isn't like they fired our boss, which they did.
sentences.zh: 所以这不只是像他们开除我们的老板那样——虽然他们的确这么做了。

sentences.en: They wiped out a large number of people.
sentences.zh: 他们清除掉了数量庞大的一批人。

sentences.en: One of the things Nick Bilton said in that ill-fated email to the staff was that he was excited to tell, I'm paraphrasing here,
sentences.zh: 尼克·比尔顿（Nick Bilton）在那封发给员工的不幸邮件中说过的一点是，他很高兴能告诉大家——我在这里换句话说——

sentences.en: he was excited to tell the staff about the new crop of correspondence.
sentences.zh: 他很高兴向员工们介绍新一批的记者阵容。

sentences.en: And when I saw that, I thought, okay, they're going to fire all of us eventually.
sentences.zh: 当我看到那个时，我想，好吧，他们迟早会把我们全都开除的。

sentences.en: That's the plan.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的计划。

sentences.en: He put it in writing for all of us to see.
sentences.zh: 他把它写成了文字，让我们所有人都能看到。

sentences.en: And so that's why I use these, admittedly for a journalist, hyperbolic terMs.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我用了这些对记者来说无可否认有些夸张的词汇。

sentences.en: They capture the scale of what happened.
sentences.zh: 它们抓住了所发生事情的规模。

sentences.en: You then do have a meeting with CBS leadership after this very contentious interaction.
sentences.zh: 在这场火药味十足的对话之后，你随后确实与哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）的高层开了会。

sentences.en: connection.
sentences.zh: 关联。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about that meeting and if you were at that point going in expecting to be fired?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我讲讲那次会议吗？当时你进去的时候，是不是就料到自己会被开除？

sentences.en: Oh, gosh.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Furthest thing from my mind.
sentences.zh: 这简直是我脑子里最不可能想到的事。

sentences.en: It hadn't occurred to me.
sentences.zh: 我根本没往那方面想。

sentences.en: The president of
sentences.zh: 时任

sentences.en: CBS News, Tom Sobrowski, sent me a note and said, can you come by and talk to us?
sentences.zh: CBS新闻部总裁汤姆·索布罗夫斯基（Tom Sobrowski）给我发了条便条，说，你能过来跟我们谈谈吗？

sentences.en: And I said, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 我说，当然可以。

sentences.en: I scheduled about an hour on my calendar for the meeting.
sentences.zh: 我在日程表上为这次会议预留了大约一个小时。

sentences.en: I didn't know who was going to be there in the meeting.
sentences.zh: 我不知道谁会去开会。

sentences.en: So I walk in the door and I see Barry Weiss is sitting in there and I think, this is terrific of her.
sentences.zh: 所以我走进门，看到巴里·韦斯（Barry Weiss）坐在里面，我想，她人真好。

sentences.en: She's come to this meeting and now I'm going to be able to ask her these questions.
sentences.zh: 她来参加这个会议了，现在我终于可以问她这些问题了。

sentences.en: She's going to be able to explain what happened.
sentences.zh: 她能解释到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: But it really didn't occur to you that you could be fired after so many of your colleagues had been let go, after you'd had this contentious interaction with your new boss?
sentences.zh: 但是在那么多同事被解雇之后，在与新老板进行了如此火药味十足的对话之后，你真的没想过自己可能会被开除吗？

sentences.en: You know, some reporter I turned out to be.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我这个记者当得还真失败。

sentences.en: I just didn't connect the dots.
sentences.zh: 我就是没把这些事联系起来。

sentences.en: I mean, was this meeting contentious?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这场会议火药味很浓吗？

sentences.en: Yes, but 60 Minutes is known for two things, a ticking stopwatch and hard questions.
sentences.zh: 是的，但《60分钟》以两样东西闻名：滴答作响的秒表和严厉的提问。

sentences.en: And we ask ourselves those hard questions in the shop because they sharpen us and make us better.
sentences.zh: 我们在内部也会这样严厉地质问自己，因为这能让我们更敏锐、变得更好。

sentences.en: There was a screening once with Mike Wallace and Mike and the executive producer and founder of 60 Minutes, Don Hewitt, got into a big argument about a script.
sentences.zh: 有一次迈克·华莱士（Mike Wallace）在审片时，《60分钟》的执行制片人兼创始人唐·休伊特（Don Hewitt）和迈克就一份剧本大吵了一架。

sentences.en: Wallace jumps up in the middle of the screening,
sentences.zh: 华莱士在审片中途猛地跳起来，

sentences.en: throws his script up in the air, and yells at Don, well, then you write the effing thing.
sentences.zh: 把剧本往空中一扔，朝唐大吼：好吧，那你来写这个他妈的东西好了！

sentences.en: One of those pieces of paper comes down and slices an associate producer across the face.
sentences.zh: 其中一张纸落下来，划破了一名助理制片人的脸。

sentences.en: He's bleeding now.
sentences.zh: 他现在流血了。

sentences.en: He's got a paper cut on his face.
sentences.zh: 他的脸上被纸划伤了。

sentences.en: That was about a story.
sentences.zh: 那次是为了一个故事。

sentences.en: The meeting that I was in was about whether 60 Minutes was going to even survive or not.
sentences.zh: 而我参加的那次会议，讨论的是《60分钟》究竟还能不能存活下去。

sentences.en: So you walk in, and what was the energy of the room?
sentences.zh: 所以你走了进去，当时房间里的气氛是怎样的？

sentences.en: Hostile.
sentences.zh: 充满敌意。

sentences.en: Dismissive.
sentences.zh: 充满轻蔑。

sentences.en: Before I could take my seat, Tom Sobrowski said, this is a firing offense.
sentences.zh: 我还没来得及坐下，汤姆·索布罗夫斯基就说，这是一个够得上被开除的行为。

sentences.en: I was confused.
sentences.zh: 我很困惑。

sentences.en: I wasn't sure who he was talking about in the room.
sentences.zh: 我不确定他在说屋里的哪个人。

sentences.en: But it became plain very quickly that they were talking about me, and they were unhappy about the meeting that had occurred.
sentences.zh: 但很快就很清楚了，他们说的是我，而且他们对刚才发生的那个会议很不满。

sentences.en: A meeting that had ended in thunderous applause for me, if I may say so, because somebody had stood up for the broadcaSt.
sentences.zh: 如果我可以这么说的话，那场会议最终是以雷鸣般的掌声为我结束的，因为有人为这个节目站了出来。

sentences.en: So I sit down, like, okay, well, let's talk about it.
sentences.zh: 所以我坐下来，心想，好吧，那我们来谈谈吧。

sentences.en: And Tom accuses me of physically abusing Nick Bilton.
sentences.zh: 然后汤姆指责我人身虐待尼克·比尔顿。

sentences.en: This is a lie.
sentences.zh: 这是个谎言。

sentences.en: I didn't come within 10 feet of Nick Bilton.
sentences.zh: 我离尼克·比尔顿十英尺近的距离都没有过。

sentences.en: In my life, I have never put my hands on anyone in anger.
sentences.zh: 我这辈子从来没有对任何人动过手，更没有带着怒气动过手。

sentences.en: Not one time.
sentences.zh: 一次也没有。

sentences.en: And when he was caught in that lie, he said, well, okay, I take that back.
sentences.zh: 当他的谎言被戳穿时，他说，好吧，我收回这话。

sentences.en: And I said, great.
sentences.zh: 我说，很好。

sentences.en: Conversation proceeded a little bit.
sentences.zh: 对话稍微继续了一下。

sentences.en: I turned to Barry Weiss, who was sitting to my left, and I said, but let's, you know, let's talk about the firings.
sentences.zh: 我转向坐在我左手边的巴里·韦斯，我说，但是，你知道的，我们来谈谈解雇的事吧。

sentences.en: Why were the firings necessary?
sentences.zh: 为什么非要进行这些解雇？

sentences.en: I'm not answering that question.
sentences.zh: 我不回答这个问题。

sentences.en: Well, how did Tanya Simon not lead the broadcast brilliantly?
sentences.zh: 好吧，塔尼亚·西蒙（Tanya Simon）怎么就不是出色地领导这个节目了？

sentences.en: I'm not answering that question.
sentences.zh: 我不回答这个问题。

sentences.en: okay, Sharon Alfonsi, Cecilia Vega,
sentences.zh: 好吧，莎朗·阿尔方西、西莉亚·维加，

sentences.en: what possible reason could there be to take them off the air?
sentences.zh: 把他们撤出荧屏能有什么合理的理由？

sentences.en: I'm not answering that question.
sentences.zh: 我不回答这个问题。

sentences.en: So now I'm detecting a pattern.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我看出规律了。

sentences.en: That's going to go nowhere.
sentences.zh: 这根本谈不出什么结果。

sentences.en: She is still going to stonewall about why she took all these people out.
sentences.zh: 她仍然会对她为什么要清洗所有人这件事采取敷衍搪塞的态度。

sentences.en: So I'm thinking that the meeting's going to carry on.
sentences.zh: 所以我以为会议还会继续开下去。

sentences.en: We're going to have a long conversation.
sentences.zh: 我们会有很长的对话。

sentences.en: I'm going to hear from them about what they think.
sentences.zh: 他们会听听我对他们的看法。

sentences.en: They're going to hear from me about what I think.
sentences.zh: 我会听听他们对我的看法。

sentences.en: The temperature in the room is low, but it's very hostile from their side.
sentences.zh: 房间里的温度不高，但从他们那一方来看，敌意非常浓烈。

sentences.en: I'm speaking about the way I'm speaking to you now.
sentences.zh: 我说话的语气就像我现在跟你说话这样。

sentences.en: Very quickly after the meeting began, Tom Sebrowski said, this conversation is over.
sentences.zh: 会议开始后没多久，汤姆·瑟布罗夫斯基就说，这次谈话结束了。

sentences.en: I was stunned.
sentences.zh: 我惊呆了。

sentences.en: And I didn't have a 60-minute stopwatch in that room.
sentences.zh: 我在那个房间里可没有带《60分钟》的秒表。

sentences.en: I don't know how long it lasted really, but I think it was about 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道它持续了多久，但我想大约是10分钟吧。

sentences.en: So they tell me, that is to say Tom Sebrowski tells me as I'm walking through the door, you'll have our answer in a few minutes.
sentences.zh: 所以他们告诉我，也就是当我正往门外走时，汤姆·瑟布罗夫斯基告诉我，几分钟后你就会得到我们的答复。

sentences.en: I went over to my office and much to my surprise, all of my guys on my team were still there.
sentences.zh: 我回到了我的办公室，让我大吃一惊的是，我团队里所有的小伙子们都还在那儿。

sentences.en: They wanted to know what happened in the meeting.
sentences.zh: 他们想知道会议上发生了什么。

sentences.en: What was that all about?
sentences.zh: 那到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Did they explain why our people were fired?
sentences.zh: 他们解释为什么我们的人被解雇了吗？

sentences.en: And I sat down in my office.
sentences.zh: 我坐在办公室里。

sentences.en: It has a big plate glass window that looks out on the newsroom.
sentences.zh: 那里有一扇可以看到新闻编辑室的大玻璃窗。

sentences.en: And there were a whole bunch of people standing out there, but I didn't think anything of it.
sentences.zh: 外面站着一大群人，但我没多想。

sentences.en: I'm waiting to find out what my fate is.
sentences.zh: 我在等著知道我的命运会是什么。

sentences.en: I explained to my team, I think I just got fired, but they haven't told me that.
sentences.zh: 我向我的团队解释，我想我刚刚被解雇了，但他们还没亲口告诉我。

sentences.en: And then I look up and all those people are still out there and the staff members.
sentences.zh: 然后我抬头一看，所有那些人以及员工们依然站在外面。

sentences.en: and I don't think anything of it.
sentences.zh: 而我还是没多想。

sentences.en: And then it hits me.
sentences.zh: 接着我突然明白了。

sentences.en: This is a vigil.
sentences.zh: 这是一场守夜。

sentences.en: An hour goes by, two hours go by, three hours go by, four hours go by, and I go back outside and said,
sentences.zh: 一个小时过去了，两个小时过去了，三个小时过去了，四个小时过去了，然后我走到外面说，

sentences.en: I'm leaving.
sentences.zh: 我要走了。

sentences.en: They've been standing out there for four hours.
sentences.zh: 他们已经在外面站了四个小时了。

sentences.en: I said, I'm leaving.
sentences.zh: 我说，我要走了。

sentences.en: You guys have got to go home to your families right now.
sentences.zh: 你们现在必须回家陪你们的家人。

sentences.en: oh, I doubt they're going to tell me tonight.
sentences.zh: 哦，我怀疑他们今晚会告诉我结果。

sentences.en: So I packed up and left just so those people would go home.
sentences.zh: 所以我收拾好东西离开了，就为了让那些人能回家。

sentences.en: And not long after that, the email came through and said that I'd been fired.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，邮件就发过来了，说我已经遭到了解雇。

sentences.en: Just to understand your position in this, you would have been open to a path forward.
sentences.zh: 为了解你在这件事上的立场，你本来是对继续前进持开放态度的。

sentences.en: You wanted to remain at 60 Minutes?
sentences.zh: 你想留在《60分钟》吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: A path forward to me was an obvious conclusion for what this meeting was going to be about.
sentences.zh: 对劳资双方而言，继续合作下去本应是这场会议水到渠成的结果。

sentences.en: That's exactly what I thought.
sentences.zh: 我当时就是这么想的。

sentences.en: And I expected them to say, look, this is why we had to fire everybody.
sentences.zh: 我本期待他们会说，听着，这就是我们不得不解雇所有人的原因。

sentences.en: I mean, your questions, Scott, are valid, and here's why we did what we did.
sentences.zh: 我是说，斯科特，你的提问是合情合理的，而这就是我们采取那些行动的原因。

sentences.en: So stay at 60 Minutes?
sentences.zh: 所以要留在《60分钟》？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: It didn't occur to me that this could happen.
sentences.zh: 我压根没想过这种事会发生。

sentences.en: But Scott, in a meeting, you accused Barry Weiss, the head of the network, of wanting to murder the
sentences.zh: 但是斯科特，你在会上指责网络负责人巴里·韦斯想要扼杀这个

sentences.en: show, of coming into 60 Minutes with the agenda to dismantle the institution, and you did not think that that was going to have repercussions that could lead to your firing?
sentences.zh: 节目，指责她带着拆散这个机构的政治意图进入《60分钟》，而你难道不认为这会产生导致你被解雇的后果吗？

sentences.en: We used to be able to have conversations like that at CBS News.
sentences.zh: 我们过去在CBS新闻部是可以进行这种对话的。

sentences.en: But the difference today is that the people running CBS News will not be questioned.
sentences.zh: 但如今的不同之处在于，管理CBS新闻部的那群人是不容许别人质疑的。

sentences.en: After the break, more with Scott Pelley.
sentences.zh: 休息过后，我们将继续对话斯科特·佩利。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘（Wynna Liu）。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏板块的字谜游戏《连线》（Connections）。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基（Sam Azersky），我每天负责创作《拼字蜜蜂》（Spelling Bee）和《字母之盒》（Lettered）游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉症的奇特感知。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 当我听音乐时我能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚刚听到的人这样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games，今天就开始游玩吧。

sentences.en: I want to take a step back because, of course, all this didn't happen in a vacuum.
sentences.zh: 我想退回一步，因为当然，所有这一切都不是凭空发生的。

sentences.en: The saga really at CBS News began when David Ellison, the son of Oracle billionaire Larry Ellison, took over CBS as part of his purchase of Paramount.
sentences.zh: CBS新闻部的这场大戏，实际上始于甲骨文亿万富翁拉里·埃里森（Larry Ellison）的儿子大卫·埃里森（David Ellison）在收购派拉蒙（Paramount）的过程中接管了CBS。

sentences.en: There was a lot of turmoil around that sale.
sentences.zh: 那次收购前后伴随着巨大的动荡。

sentences.en: The longtime previous owner of Paramount and CBS Sherry Redstone told my New York Times colleague that she sold the company to Ellison in part because after Hamas's attack on Israel on October 7th,
sentences.zh: 派拉蒙和CBS的前长期所有者谢莉·雷石东（Sherry Redstone）曾向我的《纽约时报》同事透露，她之所以将公司卖给埃里森，部分原因是在10月7日哈马斯袭击以色列之后，

sentences.en: she wanted to devote herself to causes around Israel.
sentences.zh: 她希望全身心投入到与以色列相关的公益事业中去。

sentences.en: I'm sure there were other reasons as well.
sentences.zh: 我确信还有其他原因。

sentences.en: Did you ever speak to Ms. Redstone about the sale and how did you feel about it?
sentences.zh: 你曾与雷石东女士谈过这笔收购吗？你对此作何感想？

sentences.en: I didn't speak to Sherry Redstone about the sale.
sentences.zh: 我没有和谢莉·雷石东谈过这笔收购。

sentences.en: I felt the sale was very necessary.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这笔收购是非常必要的。

sentences.en: The company was in financial trouble.
sentences.zh: 这家公司陷入了财务困境。

sentences.en: It wasn't clear what our path forward was going to be just as a company.
sentences.zh: 仅作为一家公司而言，我们未来的发展方向并不明朗。

sentences.en: Mr. Ellison came in with a lot of money behind him.
sentences.zh: 埃里森先生带着巨额资金入主。

sentences.en: A young man of vision.
sentences.zh: 一位有远见的年轻人。

sentences.en: And I thought this is going to be very good for all of us.
sentences.zh: 我当时认为这对我们所有人都大有好处。

sentences.en: The very last thing that the previous ownership did was pay a multi-million dollar bribe to the president to settle this frivolous, ridiculous lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 前任管理层做的最后一件事，就是向总统支付数百万美元的贿赂，以了结这起无聊、荒唐的诉讼。

sentences.en: And very shortly after that, somehow, the Trump administration approved the sale.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，特朗普政府不知何故就批准了这笔收购。

sentences.en: So, that lawsuit against 60 Minutes had caused a great deal of concern in 60 Minutes.
sentences.zh: 所以，针对《60分钟》的那场诉讼曾在《60分钟》内部引起了极大的担忧。

sentences.en: Paying the bribe broke our hearts.
sentences.zh: 付出行贿让我们心碎。

sentences.en: No lawyer thought that was necessary, but they did it to get the sale through.
sentences.zh: 没有律师认为那是必要的，但他们为了促成交易还是这么做了。

sentences.en: And at that point, my colleagues and I thought, great, that's behind us.
sentences.zh: 当时我和我的同事们都觉得，太好了，这页总算翻过去了。

sentences.en: We have bright new leadership with financial resources.
sentences.zh: 我们有了资金充足且耳目一新的领导层。

sentences.en: we're in better shape than we were before.
sentences.zh: 我们的状况比以前更好了。

sentences.en: That was the theory.
sentences.zh: 这只是理论上的。

sentences.en: Just to give the context here,
sentences.zh: 为了交代一下背景，

sentences.en: President Trump had sued 60 Minutes over an interview of Vice President Kamala Harris during the 2024 election.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统在2024年大选期间就《60分钟》采访副总统卡玛拉·哈里斯一事起诉了该节目。

sentences.en: As you mentioned, Paramount under Sherry Redstone settled the case, even though many legal experts believed that there was no merit to the suit.
sentences.zh: 正如你所提到的，在谢丽·雷石东的领导下，派拉蒙公司庭外和解了此案，尽管许多法律专家认为这起诉讼毫无依据。

sentences.en: And they paid $16 million to the president.
sentences.zh: 他们向总统支付了1600万美元。

sentences.en: Paramount denied that those two things were linked, that payment and then the deal going through.
sentences.zh: 派拉蒙否认这两件事有关联，即支付这笔钱和随后的交易达成。

sentences.en: And correct me if I'm wrong, am I hearing you say that you supported the sale to Ellison?
sentences.zh: 如果我没理解错的话，请纠正我，我听到的意思是您支持将公司出售给埃里森吗？

sentences.en: Had you lost confidence in the leadership of Sherry Redstone at that point?
sentences.zh: 当时您对谢丽·雷石东的领导层失去信心了吗？

sentences.en: They bribed the president to get the deal done.
sentences.zh: 他们向总统行贿以促成这笔交易。

sentences.en: So yeah, there was a massive collapse of confidence in the previous ownership.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，对前任所有者的信任彻底崩塌了。

sentences.en: So the deal goes through and Ellison takes over.
sentences.zh: 于是交易达成，埃里森接管了公司。

sentences.en: What assurances, if any, did you get from David Ellison and the new leadership that there wouldn't be interference at 60 Minutes?
sentences.zh: 您从大卫·埃里森及新领导层那里得到了什么样的保证（如果有的话），即《60分钟》不会受到干涉？

sentences.en: Did you ask for those assurances?
sentences.zh: 您要求过这种保证吗？

sentences.en: Did you speak with David Ellison?
sentences.zh: 您跟大卫·埃里森谈过吗？

sentences.en: The morning the merger was announced as complete, I was amazed that, as far as I know, the first stop that David Ellison made in his new empire was 60 Minutes, CBS News.
sentences.zh: 宣布合并完成的那个早晨，据我所知，大卫·埃里森在他的新帝国的第一个落脚点竟然是CBS新闻的《60分钟》，这让我大为震惊。

sentences.en: First thing in the morning, he's walking through the 60 Minutes offices.
sentences.zh: 一大早，他就在《60分钟》的办公室里踱步。

sentences.en: He comes and walks into my office and extends his hand and says, I'm proud to meet you, sir, he called me.
sentences.zh: 他走过来走进我的办公室，向我伸出手说：“我很荣幸能见到您，先生”——他是这么称呼我的。

sentences.en: I guess I'm just old.
sentences.zh: 我想我只是老了。

sentences.en: And I told him how wonderful it was to meet him.
sentences.zh: 我告诉他见到他是多么高兴。

sentences.en: He walked out into our newsroom and made a very nice speech about independence, about how important 60 Minutes was to the corporation writ large,
sentences.zh: 他走到我们的新闻编辑室，发表了一篇非常精彩的演讲，谈到了独立性，《60分钟》对整个公司而言是多么重要，

sentences.en: and essentially telling everybody that they were going to take care of us.
sentences.zh: 并且基本上告诉所有人，他们会照顾好我们的。

sentences.en: Um, we were walking on air.
sentences.zh: 呃，我们当时简直飘飘然了。

sentences.en: Uh, we liked him.
sentences.zh: 呃，我们挺喜欢他的。

sentences.en: Uh, he had the financial backing to back up his words.
sentences.zh: 呃，他有雄厚的资金来兑现他的承诺。

sentences.en: And we thought a bright new era was coming after all the previous difficulty.
sentences.zh: 在经历了先前的种种困难之后，我们以为一个光明的崭新时代即将来临。

sentences.en: ellison then hires barry weiss to run cbs news um weiss we should say is a former opinion writer
sentences.zh: 随后埃里森聘请巴里·韦斯来主管CBS新闻，呃，顺便说一下，韦斯曾是《纽约时报》的评论专栏作家，

sentences.en: at the new york times who left to start her own publication after claiming bias in the times
sentences.zh: 她在声称《纽约时报》评论版存在偏见后离职，并创办了自己的出版物

sentences.en: opinion section i never worked with her for the record the free press which she launched
sentences.zh: 记录在案的是，我从未与她共事过。她创办的《自由报》

sentences.en: is generally pro-israel it builds itself as pushing against what it sees as the mainstream media
sentences.zh: 大体上亲以色列，它标榜自己旨在对抗它所认为的主流媒体。

sentences.en: What did you make of her appointment?
sentences.zh: 您对她的任命有何看法？

sentences.en: I was not familiar with her name.
sentences.zh: 我以前没听说过她的名字。

sentences.en: So I did some research and discovered those things that you just outlined.
sentences.zh: 所以我做了一些调查，发现了你刚才概述的那些情况。

sentences.en: She was going to be the new editor-in-chief at CBS News.
sentences.zh: 她将成为CBS新闻的新任总编辑。

sentences.en: There never had been a title like that at CBS News.
sentences.zh: CBS新闻以前从未有过这样的头衔。

sentences.en: It's sort of a print title.
sentences.zh: 这算是印刷媒体的头衔。

sentences.en: It doesn't really translate to television, but she wanted to call herself that.
sentences.zh: 它并不真正适用于电视行业，但她自己想要这个称呼。

sentences.en: What concerned me was that she had zero television experience and had never managed a large global operation like CBS News.
sentences.zh: 让我担忧的是，她毫无电视行业经验，也从未管理过像CBS新闻这样的大型全球化运营机构。

sentences.en: Those were red flags to me, but I thought, you know, David Ellison thinks she's the right person for the job.
sentences.zh: 这些对我来说都是危险信号，但我心想，你知道的，大卫·埃里森认为她是这份工作的合适人选。

sentences.en: We are absolutely going to welcome her, listen to her, and give her the benefit of the doubt.
sentences.zh: 我们绝对会欢迎她、倾听她的意见，并给予她信任。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm surprised that you hadn't heard of her.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我很惊讶你竟然没听说过她。

sentences.en: She's a lightning rod in journalism.
sentences.zh: 她是新闻界的一个争议人物。

sentences.en: You know, she just hadn't crossed my radar.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她只是没进入我的雷达范围。

sentences.en: And if I hadn't heard of Barry Weiss at that point in time, that probably tells you more about me than it does her.
sentences.zh: 如果在那个时间点我还没听说过巴里·韦斯，那比起她来，这可能更能说明我自己的问题。

sentences.en: So when Barry comes in, she has a meeting with senior 60 Minutes staffers.
sentences.zh: 所以当巴里上任时，她与《60分钟》的高级员工举行了一场会议。

sentences.en: And in that meeting, she asked, and I'm quoting, why does the country think you're biased?
sentences.zh: 在会上，她提出了一个问题（我引述一下）：“为什么全国都认为你们有偏见？”

sentences.en: Is that a correct assessment of that?
sentences.zh: 这种说法准确吗？

sentences.en: I wasn't there.
sentences.zh: 我当时不在场。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 原来如此。

sentences.en: But that is what I've been told by my colleagues who were there, and they were shocked.
sentences.zh: 但这是当时在场的同事告诉我的，他们都惊呆了。

sentences.en: That was sort of her hello to the staff at 60 Minutes.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是她对《60分钟》员工的见面礼。

sentences.en: What was the feeling about that particular opening salvo to the team?
sentences.zh: 对于团队收到的这记开场白，大家的感受如何？

sentences.en: uh-oh.
sentences.zh: 呃哦。

sentences.en: She, I am told, said something to the effect of, why do you think the country thinks you're biased?
sentences.zh: 据我所知，她说了一些类似于“你们为什么认为全国都觉得你们有偏见？”的话，

sentences.en: But she didn't offer any kind of a metric.
sentences.zh: 但她没有提供任何衡量标准。

sentences.en: You know, what's your metric?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你们的标准是什么？

sentences.en: Why do you think so?
sentences.zh: 为什么你们会这么想？

sentences.en: Do you have a poll?
sentences.zh: 你们有民调数据吗？

sentences.en: Is there market research?
sentences.zh: 有市场调研吗？

sentences.en: What are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 你们到底在说什么？

sentences.en: Because We certainly didn't believe that.
sentences.zh: 因为我们绝对不认同那种说法。

sentences.en: And we just felt that she was making statements that perhaps she couldn't back up and was coming into the news division with hardened preconceived notions that didn't seem to be thought through.
sentences.zh: 我们只是觉得她发表的言论或许根本无法支撑，而且她带着根深蒂固的预设观念进入新闻部门，这些观念似乎根本没有经过深思熟虑。

sentences.en: You have now accused Weiss of injecting, and I'm quoting here, falsehoods and bias.
sentences.zh: 你现在指责韦斯（我这里用原话）注入了“虚假信息和偏见”。

sentences.en: This was in your parting statement into at least one of your politically sensitive stories.
sentences.zh: 这是你在离职声明中针对至少一篇政治敏感报道时说的。

sentences.en: Can you tell me the nature of that complaint?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我那个投诉的性质吗？

sentences.en: What did she specifically ask for?
sentences.zh: 她具体要求了什么？

sentences.en: What story are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 你指的是哪篇报道？

sentences.en: As I recall, that's February.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，那是二月份的事。

sentences.en: and my team and I are doing a story about the protests in Minneapolis against the ICE crackdown there.
sentences.zh: 我和我的团队正在做一个关于明尼阿波利斯抗议活动的报道，抗议当地的移民及海关执法局（ICE）镇压行动。

sentences.en: We've interviewed Senator Rand Paul, Republican, because he's going to hold hearings into this.
sentences.zh: 我们采访了共和党参议员兰德·保罗，因为他将就此举行听证会。

sentences.en: And the fact that a Republican was going to do that was quite newsworthy.
sentences.zh: 而共和党人要这么做这一事实非常具有新闻价值。

sentences.en: So we interviewed Senator Paul and then built out a story about what had happened.
sentences.zh: 所以我们采访了保罗参议员，并围绕所发生的事情做了一篇报道。

sentences.en: The killing of
sentences.zh: 关于……的杀戮事件

sentences.en: Renee Good, the killing of Alex Preddy, the protests.
sentences.zh: 蕾妮·古德之死、亚历克斯·普雷迪之死，以及抗议活动。

sentences.en: I felt it was very important to identify that the protesters themselves were being very aggressive and that they were half of these confrontations.
sentences.zh: 我觉得非常重要的一点是要指出，抗议者本身非常具有攻击性，他们是这些冲突的一半推手。

sentences.en: And so I instructed my producers to find images over the past few weeks of these protests in which we see the protesters acting aggressively.
sentences.zh: 因此我指示我的制作人们去寻找过去几周这些抗议活动的影像资料，其中能看到抗议者表现得极具攻击性。

sentences.en: We found a picture of a protester chest bumping an officer.
sentences.zh: 我们找到了一张抗议者用胸部猛撞一名警官的照片。

sentences.en: We found a picture of an officer being hit in the head with a snowball.
sentences.zh: 我们找到了一张警官头部被雪球击中的照片。

sentences.en: We culled together a lot of video of protesters screaming in the faces of officers because we were going to talk about the killing of pretty and the killing of good.
sentences.zh: 我们搜集了大量抗议者对着警察面孔尖叫的视频，因为我们要谈论普雷迪之死和古德之死。

sentences.en: And it seemed to me important to tell the audience about the entire context.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，向观众讲述完整的背景至关重要。

sentences.en: In fact, I remember writing a line in the story that said that the protesters were pushing the boundaries of what it means to peacefully assemble,
sentences.zh: 事实上，我记得我在报道中写过这样一行字，称抗议者正在突破和平集会的界限，

sentences.en: taking the language from the First Amendment.
sentences.zh: 这句话借用了第一修正案的说法。

sentences.en: And I thought we'd done a really good job with this.
sentences.zh: 我当时觉得我们这篇报道做得非常出色。

sentences.en: we also included a picture of Alex Preddy before he was killed kicking out a taillight on a police car and made a point of saying, this is Alex Preddy and this is what he did.
sentences.zh: 我们还附上了一张亚历克斯·普雷迪遇害前踢碎警车尾灯的照片，并特意指出：这就是亚历克斯·普雷迪，这就是他做的事。

sentences.en: So the story goes through screenings.
sentences.zh: 因此，这篇报道通过了审查。

sentences.en: It's very well received.
sentences.zh: 反响非常好。

sentences.en: There are notes as always, and we do rewrites as always.
sentences.zh: 一如既往地有一些意见批注，我们也一如既往地进行了重写。

sentences.en: But this is on a very tight deadline.
sentences.zh: 但这次的截稿时间非常紧迫。

sentences.en: It's Sunday.
sentences.zh: 那是星期天。

sentences.en: We're going on the air that night.
sentences.zh: 我们当晚就要播出。

sentences.en: And in the case of stories that are, as we say, crashing, meaning right against the deadline, our deadline on Sunday is noon.
sentences.zh: 对于我们所说的“紧急赶制”的报道，也就是紧贴截止期限，我们周日的截止时间是中午。

sentences.en: So we work on all of these things.
sentences.zh: 所以我们一直在处理所有这些事情。

sentences.en: We get the piece approved by everyone.
sentences.zh: 我们让所有人批准了这篇稿子。

sentences.en: And about four hours after our deadline, Barry Weiss sends an email to my boss, Tanya Simon.
sentences.zh: 大约在我们截止时间过去四个小时后，巴里·韦斯给我的老板塔尼亚·西蒙发了一封电子邮件。

sentences.en: Two of the things in the email include, can we make the protesters look more violent?
sentences.zh: 邮件中的两点内容包括：我们能把抗议者拍得更暴力一点吗？

sentences.en: Now, I'm paraphrasing.
sentences.zh: 现在，我在用我自己的话说。

sentences.en: I don't have the quote.
sentences.zh: 我没有原话引述。

sentences.en: But that's what was communicated to me.
sentences.zh: 但这就是传达给我的意思。

sentences.en: And the other thing was Renee Good's car.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是关于蕾妮·古德的车。

sentences.en: You need to describe her as driving toward the officer.
sentences.zh: 你们需要把她描述为正驾车冲向警官。

sentences.en: This is not what you see on the video.
sentences.zh: 这跟你在视频里看到的可不一样。

sentences.en: On the video, you see the officer standing slightly off the front of the car, and you clearly see Miss Good's wheels turned completely as far as they will go,
sentences.zh: 在视频中，你可以看到警官站在车头稍微偏一点的地方，并且能清晰地看到古德女士的车轮已经完全打死，打到了极限，

sentences.en: away from the officer.
sentences.zh: 方向是背离警官的。

sentences.en: But he shoots her in the head, kills her, and says something about her in that moment that I can't repeat in polite company.
sentences.zh: 但他却朝她头部开枪，打死了她，当时还说了一些我在正经场合无法复述的关于她的话。

sentences.en: So we have gone out of our way in our plan from the very beginning to show the protesters for the responsibility that they had.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们从一开始的计划中就付出极大努力，指出抗议者应承担的责任。

sentences.en: We had already scrubbed the video archives looking for those scenes, but it somehow wasn't enough for Ms. Weiss.
sentences.zh: 我们已经在视频资料库中搜寻过那些镜头，但不知为何，这在韦斯女士看来还不够。

sentences.en: the video showed that the officer wasn't standing in front of the car and she wasn't driving toward
sentences.zh: 视频显示，警官当时并非站在车前方，她也并非开车冲向

sentences.en: him but that's what the president said about that and that's the way she wanted it described to be clear there were lots of videos that showed different moments of that interaction
sentences.zh: 他，但总统就是这么说的，而她也希望按这种方式来描述。需要澄清的是，有很多视频展示了那一互动过程的不同时刻，

sentences.en: and there was a big many analyses subsequently about what exactly through those various videos had actually happened.
sentences.zh: 后来也有过很多分析，探讨通过这些不同的视频究竟发生了什么。

sentences.en: Including an excellent one by the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 其中包括《纽约时报》的一篇精彩分析。

sentences.en: The video that I showed in our piece clearly showed the officer's feet.
sentences.zh: 我在节目中展示的视频清楚地拍到了这位警官的脚。

sentences.en: So if he's standing in front of the car, you can't see his feet.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他站在车前方，你是看不到他的脚的。

sentences.en: And it very clearly showed that the wheels were turned away from him, what appeared to be the maximum turn until the wheel had stopped.
sentences.zh: 而且视频非常清楚地显示，车轮是转向背离他的方向，看起来已经转到了最大幅度，直到方向盘无法再动。

sentences.en: So you get those suggestions
sentences.zh: 于是你收到了这些建议

sentences.en: Of course, we have to reach out to a younger and younger audience.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们必须去接触越来越年轻的受众。

sentences.en: but their argument about joining the internet age is just disingenuous.
sentences.zh: 但他们关于拥抱互联网时代的论调纯粹是虚伪的。

sentences.en: It's almost as if Barry Weiss and Nick Bilton were sealed in a time capsule in 1990 and it just cracked open.
sentences.zh: 这就好比巴里·维斯和尼克·比尔顿在1990年被封存在时间胶囊里，刚刚才被打开一样。

sentences.en: They've just discovered the internet and they're running around telling everybody how important it is.
sentences.zh: 他们刚刚发现了互联网，然后到处跑着告诉所有人这有多重要。

sentences.en: At CBS News, yeah, join the fight.
sentences.zh: 在CBS新闻部，呵，加入这场战斗吧。

sentences.en: We started our first 60 Minutes online show, 60 Minutes Overtime, in 2010.
sentences.zh: 我们在2010年就创办了第一个《60分钟》网络节目《60分钟加时赛》（60 Minutes Overtime）。

sentences.en: I shoot TikTok verticals, or I used to shoot TikTok verticals on every assignment.
sentences.zh: 我拍摄垂直屏TikTok视频，或者说我过去在每个任务中都会拍摄垂直屏TikTok视频。

sentences.en: I shot material for overtime on every assignment.
sentences.zh: 我在每一个采访任务中都为加时赛拍摄素材。

sentences.en: We're there.
sentences.zh: 我们在那里。

sentences.en: We're everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我们无处不在。

sentences.en: So you don't think 60 Minutes needs to change?
sentences.zh: 所以你认为《60分钟》不需要改变？

sentences.en: My point is that 60 Minutes is constantly changing.
sentences.zh: 我的观点是，《60分钟》一直在变。

sentences.en: Constantly innovating.
sentences.zh: 一直在创新。

sentences.en: So I just find the charge that we at 60 Minutes were frozen in amber in 1968 and nothing's ever changed since then.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是觉得那种指责——说我们《60分钟》在1968年就被冻结在琥珀中，从那以后什么都没变过——

sentences.en: I find that absolutely absurd and the kind of argument that would be made by people who just don't know what we are.
sentences.zh: 我发现这绝对荒谬，这完全是不了解我们是什么样的人才会说出的言论。

sentences.en: Nick Bilton sent a very conciliatory note to the staff this past week.
sentences.zh: 过去这一周，尼克·比尔顿向员工发了一封非常具有调解意味的便条。

sentences.en: At laSt.
sentences.zh: 总算来了。

sentences.en: He promised editorial independence.
sentences.zh: 他承诺了编辑独立性。

sentences.en: He praised some of your longtime colleagues, Leslie Stahl, Bill Whitaker, John Wertham.
sentences.zh: 他赞扬了你的一些老同事，莱斯利·斯塔尔、比尔·惠特克、约翰·韦瑟姆。

sentences.en: And I just want to say my producer just told me that while we've been talking, those three released a statement that they are staying at 60 Minutes.
sentences.zh: 我只想说，我的制片人刚告诉我，在我们交谈期间，这三个人发表了一份声明，宣布他们将留在《60分钟》。

sentences.en: How does that make you feel?
sentences.zh: 这让你有什么感觉？

sentences.en: Same reason I was staying.
sentences.zh: 和我留下的理由一样。

sentences.en: We felt like—I haven't talked to them.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得——我还没和他们谈过。

sentences.en: I assume it's the same reason.
sentences.zh: 我猜理由是一样的。

sentences.en: And we have had conversations before this about staying to maintain the principles of the broadcaSt.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，我们曾就留下来以维护节目原则进行过对话。

sentences.en: If we leave, we can't help.
sentences.zh: 如果我们离开，我们就帮不上忙了。

sentences.en: And that was my opinion.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的看法。

sentences.en: There have been other times when Anderson left, when others were fired, that we could have stormed into a meeting and quit.
sentences.zh: 以前也有过其他时刻，比如安德森离开时，其他人被解雇时，我们本可以气冲冲地闯进会议室然后辞职。

sentences.en: But those very distinguished correspondents and myself did have conversations about this over time and decided that we were better working on the inside.
sentences.zh: 但那些杰出的记者和我自己确实曾为此进行过长时间的交流，并决定我们在内部发挥作用会更好。

sentences.en: And that we could influence things for the better.
sentences.zh: 而且我们能够把事情朝更好的方向引导。

sentences.en: And we did.
sentences.zh: 我们也确实做到了。

sentences.en: And it was my intention to stay and do exactly that.
sentences.zh: 我的本意就是留下来，做 exatamente 这件事。

sentences.en: Do you think, though, they can trust those assurances?
sentences.zh: 不过，你认为他们能相信这些保证吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不能。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不能。

sentences.en: I would venture to say that trust is broken.
sentences.zh: 我敢说，信任已经破裂了。

sentences.en: Do you think Barry Weiss needs to be removed?
sentences.zh: 你觉得巴里·韦斯需要被解职吗？

sentences.en: Oh, gosh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪，是的。

sentences.en: Look, she's a lovely person.
sentences.zh: 听着，她是个可爱的人。

sentences.en: And her free press organization that she founded has been very successful.
sentences.zh: 而且她创立的自由新闻机构也非常成功。

sentences.en: She's proven that.
sentences.zh: 她已经证明了这一点。

sentences.en: Great for her, but television's not her thing.
sentences.zh: 这很好，但电视不是她的专长。

sentences.en: She brings an ideology into CBS News where that is just anathema.
sentences.zh: 她把一种意识形态带进了CBS新闻，而这简直是格格不入。

sentences.en: And so it's a terrible fit.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个糟糕的搭配。

sentences.en: It's probably not her fault, but it's just a terrible fit.
sentences.zh: 这可能不是她的错，但这真的是个糟糕的搭配。

sentences.en: She doesn't know television.
sentences.zh: 她不懂电视。

sentences.en: She doesn't understand how it works.
sentences.zh: 她不明白它是如何运作的。

sentences.en: She doesn't have management experience for a large organization like CBS News.
sentences.zh: 对于CBS新闻这样的大型组织，她没有管理经验。

sentences.en: So, yes, I do think that we would be far better off without her.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我确实认为没有她我们会好得多。

sentences.en: Maybe she goes back to the free press and has a sterling career.
sentences.zh: 也许她可以回到自由新闻并拥有辉煌的职业生涯。

sentences.en: But this is like somebody walking up to me and saying, there's a 747.
sentences.zh: 但这就像有人走到我面前说，那里有一架747。

sentences.en: There are 400 people on it.
sentences.zh: 上面有400人。

sentences.en: We need you to fly it to Paris.
sentences.zh: 我们需要你把它开到巴黎。

sentences.en: I'm going to decline because I don't have a clue.
sentences.zh: 我会拒绝，因为我一窍不通。

sentences.en: And it would have been so much better if Barry Weiss had been offered this job and said, oh, that's not for me.
sentences.zh: 如果有人向巴里·韦斯提供这份工作，而她说，哦，那不适合我，那就好太多了。

sentences.en: I don't know how to do that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道怎么做那个。

sentences.en: President Trump reacted to your being fired.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统对你被解雇做出了反应。

sentences.en: Did he?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: He went on a podcast and called you a stiff.
sentences.zh: 他在一个播客节目里说你是个顽固的家伙。

sentences.en: I'm surprised that the president of the United States would bother to notice.
sentences.zh: 我很惊讶美国总统竟然会费心去注意到。

sentences.en: but okay.
sentences.zh: 但好吧。

sentences.en: Please tell me.
sentences.zh: 请告诉我。

sentences.en: I'm not aware of this.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这件事。

sentences.en: He also said you were part of this gang of stupid, crooked people that don't care about your country.
sentences.zh: 他还说你是这帮愚蠢、腐败、不关心国家的人的一部分。

sentences.en: Stupid, I can take that.
sentences.zh: 愚蠢，我能接受。

sentences.en: Stiff, yeah, probably.
sentences.zh: 顽固，是的，可能吧。

sentences.en: Don't care about the country.
sentences.zh: 不关心国家。

sentences.en: I've never worn the uniform, but I've been in combat for this country.
sentences.zh: 我从未穿过军服，但我为这个国家经历过战斗。

sentences.en: In Afghanistan and Iraq, Kuwait, been shot at, spent nights in foxholes filling up with water in the desert.
sentences.zh: 在阿富汗、伊拉克、科威特，遭过枪击，在沙漠中度过了一个个积水的散兵坑的夜晚。

sentences.en: I'm not aware that the president of the United States has ever done any of those things for his country.
sentences.zh: 我不知道美国总统是否曾为他的国家做过这些事情。

sentences.en: Please correct me if I'm wrong.
sentences.zh: 如果我错了，请纠正我。

sentences.en: You become a journalist because you love the First Amendment.
sentences.zh: 你成为记者是因为你热爱第一修正案。

sentences.en: You become a journalist because you love the country.
sentences.zh: 你成为记者是因为你热爱这个国家。

sentences.en: And while all the other descriptions that the president used about me might be applicable,
sentences.zh: 虽然总统对我的其他所有描述可能都适用，

sentences.en: not that one, there is no democracy without journalism.
sentences.zh: 但唯独这个不是，没有新闻自由就没有民主。

sentences.en: It can't be done.
sentences.zh: 这是做不到的。

sentences.en: And that is why I am a journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 这就是我成为记者的原因。

sentences.en: Last few questions.
sentences.zh: 最后几个问题。

sentences.en: You know, on Fox News, they're going to just run the parts where I'm crying and say I'm a lunatic.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在福克斯新闻上，他们只会播放我哭泣的片段，然后说我是个疯子。

sentences.en: It's the era we live in.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们生活的时代。

sentences.en: It is the era we live in.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们生活的时代。

sentences.en: Scott, you joined CBS as a reporter in 1989.
sentences.zh: 斯科特，你是在1989年加入CBS担任记者的。

sentences.en: Proudest day of my life.
sentences.zh: 我一生中最自豪的一天。

sentences.en: You know, as I was preparing for this interview, I was thinking about, in many ways, how the story of modern CBS is the story of your own career, too.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在准备这次采访时，我一直在想，在很多方面，现代CBS的故事也是你自己的职业生涯的故事。

sentences.en: When you look back, because your tenure is now over, what do you hope your departure does?
sentences.zh: 当你回首过去，因为你的任期已经结束，你希望你的离职带来什么？

sentences.en: What do you hope will happen now?
sentences.zh: 你希望现在会发生什么？

sentences.en: My hope is that the leadership of Paramount will say to themselves, okay, this isn't working.
sentences.zh: 我的希望是派拉蒙的领导层会对自己说，好吧，这样行不通。

sentences.en: We have broadcasts that almost don't get on the air.
sentences.zh: 我们的节目几乎无法播出。

sentences.en: We have respected journalists saying that there is a thumb on the scale for one political party over another.
sentences.zh: 我们有受人尊敬的记者说，有人在某个政党身上偏心。

sentences.en: We have a broadcast which is among the most important in America, the most successful in the history of all of television.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个节目，它是美国最重要的节目之一，也是整个电视史上最成功的节目之一。

sentences.en: It was doing great.
sentences.zh: 它以前做得很好。

sentences.en: So why are we making these changes?
sentences.zh: 那我们为什么要做出这些改变？

sentences.en: We need adult supervision.
sentences.zh: 我们需要成年人的监督。

sentences.en: And at the moment, we don't have it.
sentences.zh: 而目前，我们没有。

sentences.en: We have people who have been installed in these jobs who, through no fault of their own, have no experience in television.
sentences.zh: 我们有一些被安排在这些职位上的人，虽然不是他们的错，但他们没有电视经验。

sentences.en: It's not their fault.
sentences.zh: 这不是他们的错。

sentences.en: But they don't know what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 但他们不知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: And there's a subtle political bias that I've never seen at 60 Minutes before, or at CBS News before.
sentences.zh: 并且有一种微妙的政治偏见，这是我在《60分钟》或以前的CBS新闻中从未见过的。

sentences.en: And so that is my hope, a return to sanity, a return to honor, a return to courage.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我的希望，回归理智，回归荣誉，回归勇气。

sentences.en: We used to have all of those things in abundance, and now we don't.
sentences.zh: 我们过去曾拥有这一切，而现在我们没有了。

sentences.en: But we can save this.
sentences.zh: 但我们可以拯救这一切。

sentences.en: It's possible to land this plane.
sentences.zh: 让这架飞机降落是可能的。

sentences.en: But right now, CBS News, in my view, is on fire.
sentences.zh: 但现在，在我看来，CBS新闻正在着火。

sentences.en: Scott Pelley, thank you so much for coming in today.
sentences.zh: 斯科特·佩利，非常感谢你今天能来。

sentences.en: That's Scott Pelley.
sentences.zh: 那是斯科特·佩利。

sentences.en: We reached out to CBS News after this interview regarding Pelley's claims of interference on his Minneapolis story.
sentences.zh: 在这场采访之后，我们就佩利关于他在明尼阿波利斯的报道受到干预的说法联系了CBS新闻。

sentences.en: A CBS News spokesperson replied, quote, in an email, Barry made four points in the course of editorial back and forth.
sentences.zh: CBS新闻发言人在一封电子邮件中回复道，引述如下，巴里在编辑讨论的过程中提出了四点意见。

sentences.en: They had no political motivation and were proposed solely to make the piece as strong, fair and accurate as possible,
sentences.zh: 它们没有政治动机，提出这些意见纯粹是为了使报道尽可能强有力、公正和准确，

sentences.en: as is frequently the case in any newsroom that operates with collaboration.
sentences.zh: 正如任何协同运作的新闻编辑室里经常发生的那样。

sentences.en: Not everything she raised made it into the final piece, unquote.
sentences.zh: 她提出的并非所有内容都进入了最后的报道，引述结束。

sentences.en: Quote, as for the broader claims of bias, the spokesperson wrote, quote,
sentences.zh: 引述，至于关于偏见的更广泛说法，发言人写道，引述，

sentences.en: there is no credible argument to suggest Miss Weiss was putting a thumb on the scale on behalf of the administration in any instance over the past seven months,
sentences.zh: 没有任何可信的论据表明韦斯女士在过去七个月的任何情况下代表政府偏袒某一方，

sentences.en: urging reporters to get more information, to see comments from multiple perspectives, to pitch fresh stories.
sentences.zh: 敦促记者获取更多信息，查看来自多个视角的评论，推出新的报道。

sentences.en: These are the basic functions of any editor, unquote.
sentences.zh: 这些是任何编辑的基本职能，引述结束。
